question: Čerstvo zoťaté drevo môže byť až z polovice svojej hmotnosti tvorené niečím, čoho sa musí zbaviť, kým ho dáte do pece. Čím?
topic: Štiepanie a ukladanie dreva na zimu
source_excerpt: freshly cut wood has natural 60%-70% moisture content, which must come down to about 20% to burn well

extra.why_interesting: Players think of a log as solid, dry material. Learning that about half of a fresh log's weight is water explains why firewood has to dry for a year or more and why wet wood hisses and smokes in the stove.
extra.verification_notes: Green wood is roughly half or more water by weight and must be seasoned to about 15-20% moisture before burning; no competing answer or newer development found (https://fireplaceuniverse.com/what-moisture-content-firewood/).

explanation: Surové drevo môže obsahovať až okolo 50 % vody, no dobre horí až pod zhruba 20 %. Preto sa polená sušia rok aj dva a mokré drevo v peci syčí a dymí.

question: V akom počasí sa podľa skúsených drevorubačov drevo štiepi sekerou najľahšie?
topic: Štiepanie a ukladanie dreva na zimu
source_excerpt: when struck with a maul or wedge the wood will pop apart smartly. It's the difference between wood having a partial content of water vs. ice. Ice will break, water won't.

extra.why_interesting: Most people would choose a warm, dry day for hard outdoor work. In fact, frozen wood cracks apart more easily under the axe, which is part of why splitting wood is traditionally a winter job.
extra.verification_notes: Folk wisdom among woodcutters holds that frozen wood splits most easily, which matches the claimed answer; support is anecdotal forum posts, with some dissent on species dependence, and nothing newer contradicts it.

explanation: Voda v dreve zamrzne, drevo stvrdne a skrehne, takže pod sekerou praskne čisto a menej sa vláknami trhá. Preto sa na dvoroch tradične štiepalo v treskúcej zime.
